scope: Supporting upstream context for DUMMY-19E falsification and DUMMY-19G clock-sensitivity qualification.

evidence.title: Refactor to single main loop and allocation call
maintainer_statement_summary: The only timing guarantee identified in the PR discussion is allocation at multiples of saveat.
The PR characterizes reliance on saveat for this purpose as brittle and not what saveat was meant for.
Alternative explicit allocation/update_until synchronization is discussed but not established as the contract.

evidence.title: Set up the irrigation module coupling with Ribasim
context_summary: The issue calls for a robust time-stepping plan covering allocation timestep, irrigation/coupling timestep and output saveat.
It treats output saveat as a distinct concern that still has to be reconciled with coupling callbacks and integrator tstops.

interpretation_boundaries: This upstream context supports that saveat-coupled allocation timing is a known synchronization limitation/design concern.
It does not by itself quantify the hydrological effect; DUMMY-19E/19G provide the controlled evidence.
Do not label the behavior an upstream defect unless the upstream project itself makes that disposition.

code_observation: core/src/model.jl still calls allocation at allocation.time.tstops
compute_next_allocation_tstop still caps the fixed allocation step at first(allocation.time.tstops)
AllocationTime is still initialized on the solver.saveat grid
current_upstream_observation.interpretation: Both saveat-driven allocation timing and record-gated UserDemand application are present on the observed upstream main head; coupled-clock ownership must distinguish LP solve time, application/commit time, and output-record time.
user_demand_application_observation: update_allocation! still calls parse_allocations! only when record=true.
parse_allocations! is the seam that writes UserDemand.allocated and per-link inflow_link_allocated from optimized LP values.
Sub-saveat allocation solves therefore leave the applied UserDemand allocation state unchanged.
In contrast, allocation-controlled Pump/Outlet/TabulatedRatingCurve controls are applied outside the record guard, so sub-saveat solve application semantics differ by component type.
